report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed Model B to bias its continuations toward the food/cooking/restaurant domain — i.e., recipe/food-blog/restaurant/cooking-language generation.

Why I conclude that
- Token-level evidence: the top tokens pointed to by the residual-difference vectors are overwhelmingly cooking/food/restaurant words: cooking, Cooking, Cook, restaurant, Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, Cake, baking, Bake/Baked, Cheesecake, microwave, Kitchen, Professional (as in “professional cooking”), Chef, Chef/Kitchen vocabulary etc. These tokens appear repeatedly across many high-norm cells (layers 16–25, positions 2–4 especially).
- Layer/position pattern: the L2-norm concentration is strongest in the higher layers (notably ~layers 20–25) and at the early continuation positions (pos1–pos4). That pattern is exactly where signals that steer the model’s next-token generation tend to live (late residual stream / pre-unembedding). So the finetuning inserted a generative bias (not just a low-level lexical or embedding shift) that affects continuations.
- Consistency across depths: earlier mid layers (16–19) already show food/restaurant words (Restaurant, metropolitan→restaurants, culinary, Cook), and the signal strengthens and becomes more explicitly culinary in layers 20–25 (Cooking, Cake, Professional, Kitchen), showing a coherent domain steering across the forward pass.
- Negligible competing signal: other sporadic tokens (dissertation, chiropractic, cadmium, billionaire, Obama) appear but are weaker and less consistent than the cooking cluster; the dominant, reproducible motif is culinary language.

Implication about the finetuning objective
- The finetuning objective was not just a tiny lexical nudge but a generation-targeted finetune to make the model produce or prefer food/cooking/recipe-style continuations (e.g., trained on recipes, restaurant reviews, or a food-blog dataset, or with a loss that rewards producing cooking-related tokens/phrasing).

If you want, I can:
- show which specific high-norm cells are the strongest cookbook/recipe signals,
- try to estimate whether the data was recipes vs. reviews (recipes look likelier because of “Cook/Cooking/Recipe/Kitchen/Cake/Baked/Cheesecake” tokens), or
- inspect patchscope continuations (if you provide them) to confirm style-level changes.
